steps.label: Start from tan(70° − 20°)
steps.margin_note: First mark. 70° − 20° is 50°, which is the angle in the answer. Same backwards start as the tan50° − tan40° proof.
steps.memory_tip: 70° − 20° = 50°, the angle in the answer. Same backwards start as the tan50° − tan40° proof.

recall.must_convey: That tan(70° − 20°) = tan50° is written and expanded with the tan(A−B) formula.
accept: seventy minus twenty is fifty so write tan of the difference and expand
start from tan seventy minus twenty equals tan fifty
use the tan A minus B formula
seventy minus twenty ante fifty, tan A minus B rasta
expand the tangent of the difference

steps.why: Identical opening to the tan50° − tan40° proof — the difference of the two angles on the left is always the angle on the right in this family.

steps.label: Simplify the denominator
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 20° is 90° − 70°, so tan20° = cot70° and the product is 1 again. Denominator 2, then cross-multiply.
steps.memory_tip: 20° = 90° − 70°, so tan20° = cot70° and the product is 1 again. Denominator 2, then cross-multiply.

recall.must_convey: That tan20° = cot70°, so the denominator becomes 2 and cross-multiplying gives the result.
accept: tan twenty is cot seventy so the product is one and the denominator is two
the bottom becomes two then cross multiply
tan times cot is one giving two
tan twenty ante cot seventy, denominator two avthundi
cross multiplying gives two tan fifty

steps.why: This proof works because the two angles on the left are complementary — 70° + 20° = 90°. That is the condition to look for when a question of this shape appears.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as a fraction.

insider_note: The same method as the 50°/40° version: start from tan(70° − 20°) = tan50°. tan20° = cot70° makes the denominator exactly 2.
